Qualcomm released its quarterly report and forecast weaker-than-expected profits for the current quarter. Afterwards, the company's CEO told Reuters that supply constraints will cause its revenue from Apple products to decline faster than anticipated. Here are the details.

Qualcomm is "replacing Apple with data centers"

Over the past few years, Apple has been pushing forward with its plan to replace Qualcomm-made modems with its own components, building on the foundation of its 2019 acquisition of Intel's smartphone modem business.

Qualcomm, for its part, has repeatedly assured investors that the company is prepared for the loss of Apple's business. Now, CEO Cristiano Amon is warning that this decline will accelerate, partly because ongoing supply constraints will result in the company receiving a smaller share of components than expected.

Speaking to Reuters, Amon said Qualcomm "expects revenue from Apple products to decline more rapidly starting in the fourth quarter, as supply constraints will cause its share of components used in the next iPhone launch to fall well short of the previously estimated 20%."

He added that Qualcomm has been addressing the loss of Apple's business by diversifying and expanding beyond smartphones, and expects its data center segment to generate $5 billion in revenue by fiscal year 2027:

It is worth noting that Qualcomm's relationship with Apple is not limited to supplying modem components. The company also collects royalties from Apple through patent licensing, which is separate from chip sales and should continue to be collected (for now), even as Apple transitions to using its own modem technology.

In 2019, the two companies reached a settlement in their long-running litigation and signed a six-year licensing agreement. Apple later exercised an option to extend the agreement by two years, meaning it is now valid until March 2027.
